note: Screen 9 stations + Screen 10 cards. Option B = the real MER cruise configuration (MER HISTORICAL). A and C are alternatives for comparison. cost / mass / energy / stat levels are SIMULATED GAME VALUES. earth_effect stays null unless an official NASA source backs an effect on Earth (none found for these parts).

hint.text: Carries the launch loads and holds the other parts. The real MER cruise stage carried the aeroshell with the rover inside and let go of it before entering Mars's atmosphere.

options.name: LIGHTWEIGHT ALUMINUM FRAME
options.desc: A lighter frame that holds the cruise systems with less metal.
options.parts: Thin aluminum struts · basic equipment mounts
options.limitation: Less margin for the shaking and loads of launch.

options.name: MER CRUISE STAGE STRUCTURE
options.desc: Carries the launch loads, holds the cruise systems and connects to the aeroshell that protects the rover until it separates before entering Mars's atmosphere.
options.parts: Cruise stage structure and supports · aeroshell interfaces · panel and equipment mounts
options.advantage: Integrated with the real MER mission.
options.limitation: Its performance can't be compared with A/C without engineering models.

options.name: REINFORCED ALUMINUM FRAME
options.desc: A heavier frame with extra beams for more strength.
options.limitation: Extra mass needs more fuel and budget to launch.

hint.text: Makes electricity during the trip. The real MER cruise stage had its own solar panels.

options.name: REDUCED-AREA SOLAR ARRAY
options.desc: Fewer solar cells: lighter and cheaper, but less electricity.
options.limitation: Little spare power for heaters and radio.

options.name: MER CRUISE SOLAR POWER
options.desc: Makes and regulates electricity during the cruise to Mars with solar panels on the cruise stage. Not the same as the rover's own solar panels and batteries used on the surface.
options.parts: Cruise solar panels · power regulation for the cruise systems
options.advantage: Documented, integrated design for MER's trip.
options.limitation: Don't assume a separate cruise battery without specific evidence.

options.name: EXPANDED SOLAR ARRAY
options.desc: More solar cells for extra electricity.
options.limitation: Heavier and more expensive; more area to fold for launch.

hint.text: Receives commands and sends telemetry during the trip. The real MER cruise used a low-gain and a medium-gain X-band antenna.

options.name: SINGLE LOW-GAIN X-BAND
options.desc: One wide-beam antenna: it hears Earth from almost any direction, but sends little data.
options.advantage: Simple and works without precise pointing.
options.limitation: Gets weaker as Mars and Earth move apart.

options.name: MER DUAL-GAIN X-BAND
options.desc: Receives commands and sends telemetry during the trip. The X-band radio was shared with the rover carried inside: the low-gain antenna served the first weeks, the medium-gain antenna added capability as Earth got farther away.
options.parts: Cruise Low-Gain Antenna (CLGA) + Medium-Gain Antenna (MGA) · X-band link with shared electronics
options.advantage: Combines wide coverage and higher gain for different cruise phases.
options.limitation: It is the reference design, not a guarantee of better performance than any HGA.

options.name: HIGH-GAIN X-BAND
options.desc: A directional high-gain antenna with an X-band transponder, amplifier and a way to point it at Earth.
options.parts: High-Gain Antenna (HGA) · X-band transponder · amplifier · pointing mechanism or strategy
options.advantage: Higher directional gain: more data per second.
options.limitation: Needs precise pointing; swapping it in would complicate MER's spin-stabilized cruise.

hint.text: Runs the spacecraft: commands, sensors and course corrections. The MER cruise stage had a Cruise Electronics Module.

options.name: SINGLE FLIGHT COMPUTER
options.desc: One computer does everything on the cruise stage.
options.limitation: If it fails there is no backup.

options.name: MER INTEGRATED FLIGHT ELECTRONICS
options.desc: Processing and flight control for the whole spacecraft. On MER it was shared between the cruise stage electronics and the rover it carried.
options.parts: Cruise Electronics Module (CEM) · Sun Sensor Electronics Module · computing integrated with the rover
options.advantage: Shows how MER really split its flight functions.
options.limitation: The CEM is not one single processor running the whole mission.

options.name: DUAL-REDUNDANT COMPUTERS
options.desc: Two computers: if one fails, the other takes over.
options.parts: Two flight computers · cross-strapped sensor interfaces
options.advantage: A backup is ready if something fails.

hint.text: Knows where the spacecraft points, fires thrusters for course corrections and keeps parts at safe temperatures. MER spun at about 2 rpm during cruise.

options.name: SUN-SENSOR SPIN CONTROL
options.desc: Spins the spacecraft for stability and uses only sun sensors to know where it points.
options.parts: Sun sensors · small thrusters · passive thermal paint

options.name: MER SPIN & THERMAL CONTROL
options.desc: Knows where the spacecraft points, fires thrusters for course corrections and keeps parts at safe temperatures. MER was spin-stabilized: it spun at about 2 rpm during cruise.
options.parts: 5 Sun Sensors · Star Scanner · 2 thruster clusters · 2 propellant tanks · Heat Rejection System radiators
options.advantage: Proven, integrated system for stability, maneuvers and thermal protection.
options.limitation: Built for a spinning spacecraft: other parts must work while it spins.

options.name: THREE-AXIS REACTION WHEELS
options.desc: Spinning wheels inside the spacecraft turn it precisely without spinning the whole ship.
options.parts: Reaction wheels · star tracker · thrusters · radiators
options.advantage: Precise pointing (good for a narrow high-gain antenna).
options.limitation: Heavier, uses more power, more parts that can fail.

mentorTips.structure: Tip: STRUCTURE first. MER's cruise stage carried the aeroshell with the rover inside.
mentorTips.power: Tip: POWER is next. MER's cruise stage made its own electricity with solar panels.
mentorTips.comms: Tip: COMMS is next. A wide low-gain antenna plus a medium-gain antenna worked for MER's spinning cruise stage.
mentorTips.computer: Tip: the COMPUTER is next. MER split its flight electronics between the cruise stage and the rover.
mentorTips.attitude: Tip: ATTITUDE & THERMAL is last. MER spun slowly to stay stable and used radiators to shed heat.
mentorTips.done: Your build is complete! Follow the pink path to the warehouse door.
